title: Detection by finite scalar reduction for complete objects with finite shifted Hom
statement: Let l be a prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and X any scheme. Let P,Q be derived objects over the completed integral coefficient sheaf on X. Assume Q is derived complete and Hom(P[1], Res_n Red_n Q) is finite for every n >= 0. If two morphisms P -> Q have equal images under every derived scalar extension Red_n, they are equal. The reductions use exponent n+1. No constructibility or geometric base-field hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Unpack the defining completeness Roos triangle. The product for the restricted reductions is also a product for the corresponding tower objects. Match the product maps and transitions to exhibit the canonical reduction cone as a homotopy limit.

Apply the Milnor bijection using the given finite shifted Hom groups. The scalar-adjunction units are natural, so equality of the reductions gives equality of both composites with every cone leg. Injectivity of the Milnor map gives equality of the original morphisms.
